evidence_summary: The implemented E2 statistic subtracts the round-trip cost from BOTH the observed value and every permutation replicate: `observed = sum(edge) / traded - inputs.round_trip_cost` (src/etf/power.py:154) against `if perm_edge / traded - inputs.round_trip_cost >= observed` (src/etf/power.py:162); identically in the shipped verdict engine, `observed = statistics.fmean(edges) - cost * BP` (src/etf/verdict.py:126) against `if perm and statistics.fmean(perm) - cost * BP >= observed` (src/etf/verdict.py:138). The cost term is identical on both sides and cancels exactly, so the p-value cannot depend on it. The funding term cancels one step further: perm_edge = sum(p_shuffled*(r-F)) = sum(p_shuffled*r) - F*sum(p_shuffled), and sum(|p|) is invariant under a shuffle; the docstring stops one term short of noticing this ("`|p|` is preserved by a shuffle, so the cost term is constant under the null and the test is on the mean of `p * (r - F)`", src/etf/power.py:137-138). The scale of the return series cancels too, so the pre-period volatility input is inert. Consequence for the shipped engine: on a synthetic 200-day sample (n = 200 days, 153 trades) `run_e2` returns p = 0.000250, passes = True at EVERY cost band tried - 0, 3, 9, 18, 100 and 1000 bp - while mean_net falls from +1.109% to -8.891% per trade. hypothesis_or_artifact: the registered rationale for E1's form
label: DERIVED
claim_quote:
**The threshold-free form is registered deliberately: it uses every admissible
day and is the highest-powered distribution-free test available on this
sample.**
evidence_summary: The superlative carries no computation anywhere in the repository: reports/stage_a2/power.json reports E1's power at 3 assumptions x 5 cohort sizes and compares it with no alternative test. A permutation test on the Pearson correlation is equally distribution-free - the null is the same label-shuffle null, exact for any marginals - and under the generating model the registration itself adopts it is more powerful. The model is stated in the repository's own code: "Exact for a bivariate normal, which is the generating model the power simulation registers" (src/etf/power.py:50-51). Simulated at alpha_adj = 0.0253205655, one-sided, 2,000 permutation draws and 800 simulations per cell: at n = 163 and a true rank correlation of 0.18 the registered Spearman permutation test reaches 0.6238 against the Pearson permutation test's 0.6575; at n = 237, 0.8087 against 0.8250; at n = 300, 0.8625 against 0.8950 (n = 3 cells, 800 simulations each). This is the textbook 0.912 asymptotic relative efficiency of Spearman to Pearson under normality, showing up where the registration's own model puts it. It matters a little because E1's minimum N of 237 is the figure the closure is deliberately rested on - "the most favourable figure anywhere on the record" (HYPOTHESES.md:70) - and a more efficient distribution-free primary would have lowered it.

Results: Spearman 0.6238 / Pearson 0.6575 at n = 163; 0.8087 / 0.8250 at n = 237; 0.8625 / 0.8950 at n = 300.

The claim is an unsupported superlative either way.
invalidation_note: No. The repository is closed at this SHA.

hypothesis_or_artifact: the shipped per-endpoint pacing table (Amendment 1 section 2, report.md A.1 Task 2, ADR-008, docs/ACCESS.md)

claim_quote:

spacing**, the NPLExperiment pattern for an endpoint whose ceiling was not

evidence_summary: The two formulations are asserted as equivalent and are not, because observed rate is not monotone in probe spacing when the endpoint's own latency dominates. For archive.timemap the ladder recorded 5.78/min at 5.0 s spacing, 21.28/min at 2.0 s and 12.29/min at 1.0 s (reports/stage_a1/rate_ceilings.json, archive.timemap rungs, 6 requests per rung, n = 18, all HTTP 200). "Twice the fastest verified-clean spacing" (1.0 s probed) gives 2.0 s, which is the operating figure. "Half the highest verified-clean RATE" gives 10.64/min, i.e. a spacing of 5.64 s. The published table states both the rate and the pace side by side - "| `archive.timemap` | 21.28/min (n = 18) | 2.0 s |" (REGISTRATION.md:645; report.md:145) - so the collector's registered pace permits up to 30/min against a highest-ever-verified-clean 21.28/min for that endpoint, where the stated rule promises half of it. The other five endpoints are consistent under both readings (half-rate spacing against the published operating spacing): flow.table 12.17/min -> 9.86 s vs 10.0 s; archive.availability 59.92/min -> 2.00 s vs 2.0 s; venue.candleSnapshot 59.90 -> 2.00 s vs 2.0 s; venue.fundingHistory 59.91 -> 2.00 s vs 2.0 s; kraken.ohlc 58.73 -> 2.04 s vs 2.0 s. 1 of 6 endpoints disagrees, by 3.6 s.

Method: arithmetic, 60 / (rate/2) against the published operating spacing (re-run at consolidation, 2026-09-04). Result: five of six agree to 0.05 s; archive.timemap disagrees by 3.6 s, the operating pace being 2.8x faster than "half the highest verified-clean rate".
would_resolve: State the rule as the spacing rule alone ("twice the fastest spacing probed clean"), and note that for archive.timemap the observed rate fell at 1.0 s because the endpoint's own latency, not a server limit, bounded throughput.
confidence_why: HIGH on the arithmetic; the practical risk is small, since 2.0 s is still slower than the fastest spacing verified clean and every one of the 96 probes returned 200.
invalidation_note: No. The repository is closed at this SHA.
disclosure_ref: Partly - the record does say "The figures are bounded by what was probed, not by what the server would refuse" (report.md:155-156; REGISTRATION.md:638-639), which covers the ceiling question but not the disagreement between the two stated forms of the pacing rule.
